cohort: Infants with gestational ages of >= 28 weeks and no need for positive pressure ventilation, enrolled in two Norwegian hospitals.
finding: The median heart rate at 60 seconds of age was 166 (150-181) beats per minute for preterm infants and 174 (158-187) for term infants, with statistically significant but clinically limited differences between groups.
mod_finding: Term infants born using vacuum extraction, forceps or emergency Caesarean sections had significantly higher heart rates than term infants born by unassisted vaginal deliveries or planned Caesarean sections.
cross-section timing: Immediately after birth (at 60 seconds of age)
